rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate raises aggression across all seven passes while protecting mpeg2dec's hot decode loops (IDCT, motion compensation, VLC retrieval in getbits/getvlc/getblk). SUB, SPLIT, IGV, and ICALL are cheap and correctness-safe, so their weights are high on every dimension including RuntimeCost, letting them apply broadly even to performance-critical functions; this maximizes coverage of the 58-function codebase at near-zero overhead. FLA and BCF deliver the strongest control-flow obfuscation against the large dispatcher-style functions (Decode_Picture, Make_Spatial_Prediction_, form_component_predictio, main) but carry real runtime cost, so their RuntimeCost weights are held low (0.3-0.4) to bias them toward cold, high-security-value functions like header/state parsing (gethdr, systems, verify) rather than per-block decode loops. IBR sits in between with a moderate RuntimeCost weight of 0.5, giving indirect-branch diversity on medium-heat functions. DiversityGain is kept high everywhere to compound structural divergence across passes, and CorrectnessRisk weights stay at 0.7-0.9 since the round-1 result shows the pipeline tolerates the current level comfortably.
